 Virginians vote yes on reproductive freedom, same-sex marriage, voting rights amid wave of Democratic victories
 By Jessica Kronzer 
 November 3, 2026 | 
 11:01 PM 
 | 
 Follow WTOP’s team coverage of  Election 2026 online, on air at 103.5 FM or on the WTOP News app .  
 Virginians voted to enshrine protections of reproductive freedoms, voting rights and same-sex marriages in the commonwealth’s constitution during a midterm election that’s ushered a pack of Democrats to victory.
 All three proposed constitutional amendments were passed by Virginia voters.
 But the amendment that establishes a right to reproductive health care, including abortion, is already facing a legal challenge. The case will be heard in court on Nov. 13. 
 A group of Democratic incumbents defended their U.S. House seats against Republican hopefuls in Northern Virginia. But lawmakers in other parts of the state are locked in tight races that could play into the overall balance of power in Congress.
 Click here for a look at live results in Virginia. 
 Northern Virginia democrats win reelection to Congress
 Sen. Mark Warner is among the Democrats who won reelection to Congress. 
 All 11 lawmakers who represents Virginia in the U.S. House ran for reelection in the midterms.

 Democratic Reps. James Walkinshaw, Don Beyer and Suhas Subramanyam ran successful reelection campaigns to the U.S. House. 
 Rep. Eugene Vindman won reelection in the 7th District and defended his seat against a flurry of challengers, including Republican Douglas Ollivant.
 Some Republicans believed they could flip Vindman’s seat; the first-term congressman narrowly won an open seat in 2024. District 7 includes parts of Prince William, Stafford, Spotsylvania and Culpeper counties.
 But Vindman led with 59.65% the vote and Ollivant earned 37.8%, with 96% of total votes counted. 
 Most-watched races in Virginia
 The commonwealth could play a role in Democrats’ battle to flip enough congressional seats to earn a majority in Congress. Heading into the midterms, Republicans carried a 218-214 majority in the House and a narrow majority of 53-47 in the Senate.
 The most contentious congressional races are outside of the D.C. region. 
 One tight race is unfolding in District 5, which includes the cities of Charlottesville and Lynchburg in the southside of Virginia. Republican Rep. John McGuire is fighting to defend his seat against Democrat Tom Perriello. The GOP incumbent is carrying a narrow lead with 49.57% of the vote to Perriello’s 48.69% with 94.7% of votes counted as of 11 p.m.
 In the Virginia Beach area, Republican Rep. Jen Kiggans is running against Democrat Elaine Luria in District 2.
 Out in the Richmond-area suburbs, Republican Rep. Rob Wittman is running against Democrat Shannon Taylor, Henrico County’s top prosecutor in District 1.
 Big wins for congressional Democrats in Northern Virginia 
 Walkinshaw took home 71.48% of the vote and Republican Arthur Purves fell far behind with 26.61% in the 11th District, which encompasses Fairfax City and part of Fairfax County, The Associated Press reported at 10 p.m. with 56% of total votes counted.
 Walkinshaw was first elected to Congress last year in a special election to fill a seat vacated by his former boss, the late Rep. Gerry Connolly. 
 Nearby in District 10, Subramanyam defeated Republican challenger Dave Beckwith, an Air Force veteran. With about 80% of votes counted, Subramanyam earned 199,376 votes in District 19 and Beckwith walked away with 122,815 votes, The Associated Press reported at 8:10 p.m.
 Subramanyam’s district includes Loudoun, Fauquier and Rappahannock counties; the cities of Manassas and Manassas Park, as well as parts of Prince William and Fairfax counties. He filled an open seat vacated by Rep. Jennifer Wexton in 2025. 
 Beyer handily secured a win for Democrats in Virginia’s 8 th District, defeating Republican nominee Tony Sabio, a security expert. Beyer stands out as the longest-serving congressman in Northern Virginia’s delegation, having served six terms in Congress. He earned about 78% of the vote and Sabio fell behind with 18.57%, as of 8:10 p.m. and with 23% of total votes counted.
 Almost immediately after polls closed at 7 p.m., The Associated Press called the senate race for the Warner, who brushed off a challenge from Republican Bert Mizusawa. Warner has said it will be his fourth and final term in the Senate.
 The Democratic incumbent walked away with more than 1.9 million votes and Mizusawa earned about 1.2 million8 votes, The Associated Press reported at of 10:35 p.m. with 86% of votes counted. 
 Warner’s tenure in Congress goes back to 2009; he’s the vice chair of the Senate Democratic Caucus and the Senate Intelligence Committee. Mizusawa is a retired major general of the U.S. Army.
 Changes ahead for Virginia’s constitution
 Virginians voted in favor of three questions that proposed changes to the state’s constitution.
 The first ballot measure asked about establishing a right to reproductive freedom, including abortion. An advocacy group has filed a legal challenge to block the certification of the referendum results and argued the ballot language was misleading and improperly filed. 
 The second ballot measure will replace an existing ban on same-sex marriage with language that requires all legal marriages to be treated equally under the law, regardless of either person’s sex, gender or race.
 The marriage ban isn’t enforced, thanks to a U.S. Supreme Court ruling from 2015. But proponents of the amendment argued the protection could become necessary should the Supreme Court ever overturn its prior decision.
 The final question posed to Virginia voters will expand voting rights.
 Under the approved amendment, people convicted of a felony will automatically regain their right to vote after leaving incarceration. The same measure will update the constitution to specify that a court must find a person lacks the capacity to understand the act of voting to strip them of their voting rights.
 Special election
 Democrat Sonia Ruth Vasquez Luna has won a special election to serve District 20 in Virginia’s General Assembly. She will fill an open seat vacated by Del. Michelle Maldonado in the House of Delegates.
 Vasquez Luna carried 68.19% of the vote and Republican Nathaniel Fritzen Fritzen earned 31.58% of the vote, with 84% of total votes counted as of 9 p.m.
 District 20 encompasses Manassas City, Manassas Park City and parts of Prince William County.

 Democrats win in South Carolina and North Carolina as they aim to retake Senate
 By The Associated Press 
 November 3, 2026 | 
 10:39 PM 
 | 
 WASHINGTON (AP) — Democrat Annie Andrews has won an upset victory over Republican Darline Graham for a Senate seat in South Carolina, a sign that dissatisfaction with President Donald Trump has seeped into even some of the most conservative states. 
Andrews’ victory is a defeat for Trump, who backed Graham despite doubts within his party, and it puts Democrats one seat closer to the four they need to retake control of the chamber. Democrats have also flipped a seat in North Carolina and won key races in Georgia and New Hampshire on Tuesday as they tried to recapture majorities in Congress and break Republicans’ unified hold on power in Washington.
Graham was appointed to the Senate in July after her brother, Republican Sen. Lindsey Graham, died unexpectedly, and she decided to run for a full term of her own. Andrews, a doctor, will be the first woman elected to the Senate from South Carolina. She’s the first Democrat to win a Senate seat in the state in more than 20 years.
Democrats who once saw the political map as an almost impossible lift are now hopeful that a Senate majority is within reach, even though their path runs through several more conservative states.
